 There's a good chance that when the 2026-27 NBA schedule came out, the New York Knicks and Cleveland Cavaliers circled Saturday night's game at Rocket Arena as a big one. The last time these teams met, Jalen Brunson and the Knicks closed out a dominant four-game sweep of Cleveland in the Eastern Conference Finals.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Knicks, of course, went on to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals to win the franchise's first championship in more than 50 years. Both teams are expected to be serious contenders this season, though neither has gotten off to a particularly great start. New York has had a few nights off after a Wednesday night rout of the Chicago Bulls evened their record at 4-4. This is the second straight grudge match for the Cavaliers: They had a 4-4 record going into last night's game vs. Philadelphia 76ers and LeBron James — the former Cav who the team unsuccessfully tried to bring back this past offseason.
